question: At what training compute is a general-purpose AI model classified as general-purpose under the Commission guidelines (10^23 FLOPs)?

before.answer:
The indexed documents do not cover a training compute threshold of $10^{23}$ FLOPs for general-purpose AI models. Under the AI Act, a general-purpose AI model is instead presumed to have high-impact capabilities and be classified as having systemic risk when the cumulative amount of training computation is greater than $10^{25}$ FLOPs.

[ai_act_consolidated_2026-07-27 | Article 51(2)]

This matter should be checked by a legal professional.

after.answer:
Under the Commission guidelines, an indicative criterion for a model to be considered a general-purpose AI model is that its training compute is greater than $10^{23}$ FLOP and it can generate language (text or audio), text-to-image, or text-to-video [guidelines_gpai_C2025-7719 | paragraphs (17)–(19)].
